title: Analyze bounded feedback
scope: One bounded P-control integrator step, not general PID

items.prompt: A wheel-speed loop is modelled as a toy integrator: speed y (m/s) updates as y_next = y + h·u with step h=0.1 s. A P controller commands u = clip(kp·(r - y), -L, L) with kp=2 and limit L=1.5 m/s². Current speed y=1.6 m/s, reference r=2 m/s. Compute the applied command u and the next speed y_next. Answers are graded within ±0.001.
items.solution: Raw command = 2·(2 - 1.6) = 0.8 m/s², which is inside the limits, so the clip does not change it: u = 0.8 m/s². y_next = 1.6 + 0.1·0.8 = 1.68 m/s. The clip acts on the actuator command, not on the speed.
hints: The speed is just below the reference, so expect a small positive command; check whether it stays inside the ±limit.
First evaluate the raw command kp·(r - y) = 2·(2 - 1.6); next compare it with the limits ±1.5 to get the applied u, and only then step the integrator with h = 0.1 s.

Raw command = 2·(2 - 1.6) = 0.8 m/s², which is inside the limits, so the clip does not change it: u = 0.8 m/s². y_next = 1.6 + 0.1·0.8 = 1.68 m/s. The clip acts on the actuator command, not on the speed.
items.remediation: If you got u = -0.8, you used y - r instead of r - y. Recompute y_next from the applied u. Revisit /lessons/C01.

items.prompt: A wheel-speed loop is modelled as a toy integrator: speed y (m/s) updates as y_next = y + h·u with step h=0.2 s. A P controller commands u = clip(kp·(r - y), -L, L) with kp=1.5 and limit L=2 m/s². Current speed y=0.4 m/s, reference r=3 m/s. Compute the applied command u and the next speed y_next. Answers are graded within ±0.001.
items.solution: Raw command = 1.5·(3 - 0.4) = 3.9 m/s², which is beyond +2, so the applied command is clipped: u = 2 m/s². y_next = 0.4 + 0.2·2 = 0.8 m/s. The clip acts on the actuator command, not on the speed.
hints: The speed is far below the reference, so the raw command is large and positive; the upper limit may bind.
First evaluate the raw command kp·(r - y) = 1.5·(3 - 0.4); next compare it with the limits ±2 to get the applied u, and only then step the integrator with h = 0.2 s.
Raw command = 1.5·(3 - 0.4) = 3.9 m/s², which is beyond +2, so the applied command is clipped: u = 2 m/s². y_next = 0.4 + 0.2·2 = 0.8 m/s. The clip acts on the actuator command, not on the speed.
items.remediation: If you got u = 3.9, you skipped the clip; if you got u = -2, you used y - r instead of r - y. Recompute y_next from the applied u. Revisit /lessons/C01.

items.prompt: A wheel-speed loop is modelled as a toy integrator: speed y (m/s) updates as y_next = y + h·u with step h=0.25 s. A P controller commands u = clip(kp·(r - y), -L, L) with kp=0.8 and limit L=1.2 m/s². Current speed y=2.5 m/s, reference r=-1 m/s. Compute the applied command u and the next speed y_next. Answers are graded within ±0.001.
items.solution: Raw command = 0.8·(-1 - 2.5) = -2.8 m/s², which is beyond -1.2, so the applied command is clipped: u = -1.2 m/s². y_next = 2.5 + 0.25·(-1.2) = 2.2 m/s. The clip acts on the actuator command, not on the speed.
hints: The reference is negative and below the current speed, so the error r-y and the command are negative; the lower limit may bind.
First evaluate the raw command kp·(r - y) = 0.8·(-1 - 2.5); next compare it with the limits ±1.2 to get the applied u, and only then step the integrator with h = 0.25 s.

Raw command = 0.8·(-1 - 2.5) = -2.8 m/s², which is beyond -1.2, so the applied command is clipped: u = -1.2 m/s². y_next = 2.5 + 0.25·(-1.2) = 2.2 m/s. The clip acts on the actuator command, not on the speed.
items.remediation: If you got u = -2.8, you skipped the clip; if you got u = 1.2, you used y - r instead of r - y; if you got u = 0, you clipped to [0, L] instead of [-L, L]. Recompute y_next from the applied u. Revisit /lessons/C01.

items.prompt: Toy thermal integrator: temperature y=6 °C, target r=2 °C. The applied heating/cooling rate is u = clip(1.5·(r - y), -2, 2) °C/s and y_next = y + 0.1·u (one 0.1 s step). No heat-loss model is included; negative u means cooling. Compute the signed applied u and y_next. Answers are graded within ±0.001.
items.solution: r - y = -4 °C; raw command 1.5·(-4) = -6 °C/s, which is beyond -2, so the applied command is clipped: u = -2 °C/s. y_next = 6 + 0.1·(-2) = 5.8 °C. The actuator clips the control input, not the state.
hints: The temperature is above the target, so the error r-y is negative and the actuator must cool; the cooling limit may bind.
Error r - y = 2 - 6 = -4 °C. Next multiply by 1.5 to get the raw command, compare it with ±2 to get the applied u, then take one 0.1 s step.
r - y = -4 °C; raw command 1.5·(-4) = -6 °C/s, which is beyond -2, so the applied command is clipped: u = -2 °C/s. y_next = 6 + 0.1·(-2) = 5.8 °C. The actuator clips the control input, not the state.
items.remediation: If you got u = -6, the clip was skipped; if you got u = 2, the error sign was flipped (use r - y). Revisit /lessons/C01.

items.prompt: Toy thermal integrator: temperature y=7 °C, target r=5.9 °C. The applied heating/cooling rate is u = clip(1.5·(r - y), -2, 2) °C/s and y_next = y + 0.1·u (one 0.1 s step). No heat-loss model is included; negative u means cooling. Compute the signed applied u and y_next. Answers are graded within ±0.001.
items.solution: r - y = -1.1 °C; raw command 1.5·(-1.1) = -1.65 °C/s, which is inside ±2, so it is applied unchanged: u = -1.65 °C/s. y_next = 7 + 0.1·(-1.65) = 6.835 °C. The actuator clips the control input, not the state.
hints: The temperature is only slightly above the target: the command is negative, and you must check whether it reaches the -2 limit.

items.remediation: If you got u = 1.65, the error sign was flipped (use r - y). Revisit /lessons/C01.
